title: The ABODE Study for Patients Undergoing Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy
official: At-home Breast Oncology Care Delivered With E-health Solutions - The ABODE Study for Patients Undergoing Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy
summary:
Over 12,000 women in Ontario will be diagnosed with BC this year. The COVID-19 pandemic changed the healthcare system, making it important to have high-quality virtual (online) care. Mobile health, which means getting health services on your phone, has become a common part of healthcare.

A previously developed app will be used in this study to improve the virtual care experience for BC patients that will be undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy. With this app, patients can:

* Get personalized resources that can help them navigate through the stages of their treatment.
* Access vetted information about their cancer \& treatment from a health library.
* Receive surveys about their health and well-being.
* Get mental and social support from an e-coach, who are volunteers trained to help and support patients. The e-coaches will provide information, listen to how participants are feeling, and help participants find information they might need.
* Connect with a physiotherapist to discuss healthy living and wellness.

Participants will be randomly put into one of two groups: one group will use the app, while the other will continue to get usual care without the app. Participants will have access to the app for 12 months. They will be asked about their experience, how they are feeling, and their health status at several timepoints.

At the end of the study, the two groups will be compared to see how active and engaged participants are in their treatment and see how this changes over 12 months. The study team will also examine how participants are feeling emotionally and their overall quality of life. Health service utilization data and chart review will be used to examine how patients used health services over the course of their treatment. Qualitative interviews will be conducted for some patients about their treatment and experience on the app, using photos that they submit throughout the study.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Females (assigned female at birth)\*
* Diagnosed with primary invasive BC and receiving curative intent treatment
* Must have neoadjuvant chemotherapy as their first step in treatment
* Receiving systemic therapy at UHN
* Age≥18
* Access to an electronic device with connection to the internet
* A valid email address
* Can communicate in English

Exclusion Criteria:

* Males (assigned male at birth), as BC surgical treatment options and experiences are different
* Diagnosed with non-operable breast cancer
* Stage 4/metastatic (whether determined at diagnosis or during surgery)
* Those with hearing or visual challenges
* Should not be enrolled in any other UHN study using an e-Health application
